High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is the first application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.497/2023 registered at Police Station Hanumana, District Mauganj (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376, 376(2)(N) of IPC and Section 5/6, of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 17.07.2024.

2. As per the prosecution story, the allegations against the applicant is that he taken away the minor prosecutrix with him and committed rape upon her, therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He is in custody since 17.07.2024.
Prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Sections 161 & 164 of Cr.P.C stated that she herself went with the applicant on her own free will.
Charge-sheet has been filed.
There are no criminal antecedents of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12230 2 MCRC-10258-2025 applicant.
The conclusion of the trial will take considerable time, therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the bail application and prayed for it's rejection.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

sentences.text: It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE SN Rangnath @ Ranglal Kol vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10514047/
